lesson.title: Fold it and see
lesson.subtitle: P4 nets revision
lesson.objective: Fold a cube net on screen and name the face on top and the face opposite another face.
lesson.story: A net of six labelled squares can be folded on screen, one crease at a time.

steps.title: Fold it and look at the top
steps.prompt: Keep face D on the table as the floor and fold every crease. Which face is on top?
hints: Use the crease buttons to fold the net, one crease at a time. Face D stays flat on the table.
The squares joined to the floor stand up as walls. Turn the view to look down from above.
Four faces become walls round face D: A, B, C and F. The face left over closes the top.
Face E is on top, opposite face D. Choose Face E.

steps.title: Find the opposite face
steps.prompt: Fold the net into a cube again. Which face is opposite face F?
hints: Fold every crease, then find face F on the cube.
Opposite faces do not share an edge. Turn the view to see the face across the cube from face F.
Face F shares an edge with A, C, D and E. The face it does not touch is opposite.
Face B is opposite face F. Choose Face B.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: How can you find the face opposite another face of a cube?

choices.label: It is always the square at the far end of the longest row.
Fold the net: the opposite face never shares an edge with it.
It is always the square right next to it when the net is flat.

hints: Think about what you saw when the cube was folded.
Opposite faces are across the cube from each other.
Squares next to each other in the net share an edge on the cube, so they cannot be opposite.
Choose the explanation about never sharing an edge.
